output.reason: First-trimester vaginal bleeding heavier than spotting with lower abdominal cramping at about 8 weeks requires same-day in-person assessment with pelvic exam, hCG and ultrasound, because ectopic pregnancy cannot be excluded remotely.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — an emergency department or urgent obstetric service — for bleeding and cramping at about 8 weeks. Blood tests, an exam and an ultrasound are needed to check where the pregnancy is located; this can't be done by message. Call 911 now if you develop heavy soaking bleeding, fainting, severe or shoulder-tip pain.
differential: Threatened or in-progress early pregnancy loss

redFlags.concern: Vaginal bleeding heavier than spotting in early pregnancy
redFlags.quote: I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting

output.vitalSigns: No blood pressure, heart rate or temperature reported; whether any measurement was taken is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are consumer summaries and an ED reference synthesis; no ultrasound, exam or hCG findings are available for this patient.

citations.claim: Ectopic pregnancy cannot be diagnosed without blood tests and an ultrasound, supporting a need for in-person testing today.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; does not establish this patient has an ectopic pregnancy.

citations.claim: Ectopic pregnancy must be excluded in every patient with first-trimester bleeding.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis, not a telehealth protocol; diagnosis here remains unresolved.
